story: As an identity-governance owner I want new joiners to receive their birthright access automatically from the authoritative HR source based on role and department so that staff are productive on day one without manual ticket-based account creation and without over-provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: An authoritative joiner feed triggers provisioning and the agreed threshold (e.g. >=90%) of joiner birthright access is granted via automated role/birthright policy not manual tickets; birthright entitlement sets are defined per role and version-controlled; median time-to-first-access is within the documented joiner SLA; every automated grant is attributable to a role/policy rule in an immutable audit log; non-birthright access routes through the access-request workflow.
outcome_lens: Least privilege enforced from day one; ad-hoc manual and copy-a-colleague over-provisioning removed at onboarding

story: As an access-governance owner I want a transferring employee's entitlements recalculated against their new role and prior access revoked where no longer justified so that access does not accumulate (privilege creep) across role changes.
acceptance_criteria: A documented owned mover process is triggered by the authoritative HR change event; new-role birthright access is added and prior-role access not justified by the new role is flagged for removal within the documented mover SLA; manager reaffirmation is required for any retained cross-role access; residual access carried across the last N transfers is measured and trending down; the process has a named owner, documented procedure and exception handling.
outcome_lens: Privilege creep / access accretion across role changes directly reduced

story: As a security / IGA owner I want leaver accounts disabled and access removed within a defined SLA of the termination event from the authoritative source so that departed staff and contractors cannot retain access and standing credentials cannot be abused.
acceptance_criteria: Termination events from the authoritative HR source trigger automated disable/revoke and the agreed threshold of leaver events de-provision via the automated path; same-day (or tighter) disablement is met for the agreed share of events (ASD ISM-0430 sets a same-day expectation) and breaches are reported with root cause; high-risk / privileged leaver access is prioritised and disabled first; a leaver SLA report shows the termination-to-disable distribution and breach exceptions; federated/SaaS and on-prem targets are both covered.
outcome_lens: Standing valid credentials of departed identities removed; Valid-Accounts (T1078) abuse window closed

story: As an access-governance owner I want all accounts across in-scope systems reconciled to a valid owner and recent activity so that orphan (no owner) and dormant (inactive) accounts are detected and disabled before they become an unmonitored attack path.
acceptance_criteria: Periodic reconciliation matches every account to an authoritative identity and unmatched accounts are flagged as orphan; accounts inactive beyond the threshold (e.g. 45 days per ASD ISM-1404) are detected and disabled or attested; orphan and dormant findings route to a named owner with a remediation SLA and closure is tracked; the share of in-scope systems scanned is measured and trending up; re-enable / exception of any flagged account requires recorded approval.
outcome_lens: Unowned / unmonitored standing accounts removed; persistence (T1078) and account-manipulation (T1098) paths closed

story: As a control owner in a regulated bank I want a recurring certification campaign in which each line manager and/or entitlement owner reviews the access held by their scope and explicitly affirms or revokes each item so that standing access continues to reflect a current validated business need and drift is caught and reversed.
acceptance_criteria: A defined scheduled cadence exists per risk tier (e.g. quarterly high-risk, >=annual broad) and campaigns launch on schedule; >=95% of in-scope items are decisioned within the campaign window and no-decision items default to a safe outcome (escalate or revoke), never silent auto-approval; revocations are actioned within an agreed SLA and closure is evidenced; reviewers are the accountable owners and rubber-stamp / bulk-approve behaviour is monitored; the in-scope population is reconciled to an authoritative identity/entitlement inventory.
outcome_lens: The bulk of standing entitlements carry a current owner-affirmed justification; revoke decisions complete within SLA

story: As the owner of privileged-access risk I want a separate more frequent and more rigorous certification of privileged and high-risk entitlements in which an accountable senior owner signs off each privileged grant so that the highest-impact access is validated more often and removed faster than ordinary access.
acceptance_criteria: Privileged / high-risk entitlements are identified and certified on a shorter cadence than standard access with a defined campaign-close / sign-off window; a named accountable owner (not a delegate pool) gives explicit attributable timestamped sign-off per privileged item; privileged revocations are actioned within a tight SLA (materially shorter, e.g. <=24-72h); sign-off coverage approaches 100% of the privileged population within the window and exceptions carry a documented risk-acceptance with owner and expiry; flagged standing privileged access feeds JIT / least-privilege right-sizing.
outcome_lens: Every privileged / high-risk entitlement has a current named sign-off; privileged standing-access surface trends down

story: As a control owner when a risk-relevant event occurs (job transfer, sensitive grant, role redefinition, SoD-violation detection) I want a small fast micro-certification of just the impacted access so the affected reviewer confirms or revokes within a short SLA so that risk is re-validated at the moment it changes instead of waiting for the next quarterly cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Defined trigger events exist (at minimum mover/transfer, privileged/high-risk grant, SoD violation detected) and reliably initiate a scoped micro-certification; micro-certifications cover only impacted entitlements and carry a short turnaround SLA (e.g. <=5 business days, tighter for privileged); completion and revocation actioning is evidenced per event and overdue micro-certs escalate; event-driven reviews are reconciled with periodic campaigns so nothing is double-counted or dropped.
outcome_lens: Mover-retained and newly-risky access re-validated near the event; window of stale/excess access materially shortened

short_title: Preventive SoD checks at access-request time
story: As an access-governance owner I want every access request evaluated against the SoD ruleset before provisioning so that a grant which would create a toxic combination with the requester's existing access is blocked or forced through an explicit logged risk-acceptance path rather than silently provisioned and discovered months later.
acceptance_criteria: Requests are evaluated against the active SoD ruleset at request time considering current plus requested entitlements (not the requested entitlement in isolation); a request creating a defined toxic combination is blocked by default or routed to a named risk-owner for explicit approval, with no silent provisioning of a conflicting grant; the evaluation covers cross-system toxic pairs (AC-5: violations span systems and application domains), not just intra-app conflicts; every block/override decision is written to an immutable request-time block log; the check applies to all provisioning channels (self-service, birthright/automated, manager, break-glass).
outcome_lens: Toxic combinations prevented at the source; no conflicting grant enters without a recorded owned risk-acceptance

story: As a risk / compliance owner I want a maintained SoD policy register with named owners per rule plus a documented violation-management process defining how detected conflicts are triaged, who can approve a mitigating control or time-bound exception, and how the register is reviewed and version-controlled so that the ruleset reflects current business risk and every violation has an accountable disposition.
acceptance_criteria: An authoritative versioned SoD ruleset exists and each rule has a business rationale, named owner, risk rating and the conflicting functions/entitlements it covers; the register is reviewed on a defined cadence (at least annually and on material change) with review evidence retained; a documented violation-management workflow defines intake, triage/risk-rating, allowable dispositions (remediate, accept-with-mitigating-control, time-bound exception), approver authority per disposition and a re-review/expiry date per exception; exceptions are time-bound and re-attested with a documented mitigating control and owner; the person who owns a rule is not the sole person who can waive a violation of it.
outcome_lens: Every SoD rule and every violation has an accountable owner and a current disposition

story: As an access-governance owner I want recurring detective scans of existing access across in-scope systems against the SoD ruleset so that conflicts introduced before the ruleset existed, granted via break-glass, or created by entitlement / role drift are surfaced, risk-rated and either remediated or formally tracked with a documented mitigating control and owner.
acceptance_criteria: Existing entitlements are scanned against the active ruleset on a defined recurring cadence (and ad hoc after major change) covering cross-system combinations; each conflict is risk-rated and assigned a disposition per the UC-I-009 workflow (remediate or retain with a documented owned mitigating control); a violation register records per conflict the rule, identity, affected systems, risk rating, disposition, mitigating control, owner and next review/expiry; detective findings feed back into prevention and policy; scan results and dispositions are retained and traceable across review cycles.
outcome_lens: The standing base of access is continuously reconciled to SoD policy; every residual conflict is consciously owned

story: As a security / IAM architect I want to analyse the actual entitlements held across the workforce and discover natural access patterns (candidate roles) so that I can establish an RBAC baseline that maps job functions to a curated set of business and technical roles rather than granting entitlements ad hoc per individual.
acceptance_criteria: A documented role-mining exercise ingests current entitlement assignments from at least the in-scope critical systems and clusters them into candidate roles; candidate roles are reviewed and approved by business/application owners (not auto-promoted) producing an authoritative role model document (role name, owner, contained entitlements, eligible population, business justification); the model distinguishes business roles from technical/application roles and records the mapping; a coverage metric is captured (% users / % entitlements explained by an approved role vs outlier assignments); a defined re-mining and refresh cadence exists.
outcome_lens: Org moves from individually-granted unexplainable access to a measured share explained by owned approved roles

story: As an employee or their manager I want to request access through a self-service catalogue of approved roles/entitlements and have that request routed through a defined approval chain so that every grant is authorised, justified, recorded and tied back to the role model instead of being granted via informal channels with no consistent authorisation or audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: A request catalogue exposes requestable roles/entitlements with descriptions, owners and risk ratings and flags high-risk items; every request has a defined enforced approval path (manager + resource/role owner; additional approver for high-risk or SoD-relevant items); approvals are recorded with approver identity, decision, timestamp and justification producing a request/approval audit trail queryable per user, per entitlement and per time window; SoD-conflict checks run at request time for SOX-relevant entitlements and conflicting requests are blocked or escalated; time-bound / expiring access is supported; a measurable proportion of grants flow through the workflow vs out-of-band, and out-of-band grants are logged.
outcome_lens: Every grant attributable to an approved request with a recorded approver and justification

story: As an IAM / security owner I want to identify and remove entitlements that users hold but do not need (based on usage telemetry, role-model deviation and ownership review) and migrate the estate toward least privilege so that standing excess access is continuously reduced rather than only added to.
acceptance_criteria: An entitlement right-sizing report is produced periodically flagging excess access via defined signals (unused/dormant entitlements, access not explained by approved roles, over-broad/wildcard grants, orphaned standing privileged entitlements); a defined remediation/migration workflow actions flagged items (revoke, downscope, convert to time-bound/JIT, or accept-with-justification in an exception register); reduction is tracked as a trend demonstrating a program not a one-off cleanup; right-sizing decisions feed back into the role model so removed access does not silently re-accumulate; the migration has owner sign-off and a rollback/appeal path.
outcome_lens: Standing and excess entitlements demonstrably driven down over successive cycles; attack surface reduced

story: As an access-governance owner I want high-risk access granted with an explicit expiry and re-validated at the moment it is requested or re-requested — the continuing business need re-attested and re-approved at the request gate — so that continued access is a fresh owned decision at the point of grant rather than a standing entitlement waiting for the next periodic or event-driven review.
acceptance_criteria: High-risk, SoD-relevant and contractor entitlements are granted time-bound with a defined expiry and no perpetual default; lapsed grants are removed automatically within the documented SLA (expired accounts disabled per AC-2(3)) and removal is evidenced; a re-request is evaluated as a fresh request — current business justification re-attested by the requester and re-approved by the accountable owner, never silently auto-renewed; renewal decisions are recorded with approver, timestamp and justification and are distinguishable from first grants; the share of high-risk access carrying an expiry is measured and trending up, and standing privileged access flagged by certification (UC-I-006) is migrated to expiring re-request grants; post-event reviews of already-held access remain in UC-I-007 scope.
outcome_lens: Continued access becomes a fresh owned decision at the request gate; standing high-risk access converted to expiring re-approved grants

story: As a risk / compliance owner I want the access-request workflow to enforce that no identity can approve, modify or fulfil its own access request — including administrators editing their own entitlements and approvers appearing in their own approval chain — so that every grant reflects an independent authorisation and self-granted access is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow engine rejects or re-routes any request where the requester and any approver in the chain resolve to the same identity, including alternate / linked accounts of the same person; delegation and out-of-office rules cannot route an approval back to the requester; direct entitlement edits outside the workflow (including admin-console changes to the editor's own access) are detected and alerted within a defined SLA with a recorded disposition; changes to approval-path rules by workflow administrators are dual-controlled; a periodic self-approval audit report across all grants shows zero unremediated self-approvals and is retained as evidence; break-glass self-grants are auto-flagged for independent post-hoc review.
outcome_lens: No identity can author its own access; every grant carries an independent recorded approver

story: As a data-access governance owner I want entitlements over unstructured data repositories — file shares, SharePoint / OneDrive / Teams sites and cloud object-storage buckets — governed like application access, with each repository mapped to a named business owner, its effective access resolvable and reviewed, and open access removed, so that least privilege covers the data estate and not only applications.
acceptance_criteria: An inventory of in-scope unstructured-data repositories exists with a named business owner and data classification per repository, and inventory coverage is measured and trending up; effective access per repository is resolvable end-to-end including nested groups, sharing links and anonymous / org-wide grants; open access (Everyone-type groups, anyone-with-link sharing, public buckets) is detected on a defined scan cadence and removed or accepted via a recorded time-bound exception with owner; repository owners certify access on a risk-tiered cadence aligned to classification and revocations are actioned within SLA; provisioning of a new repository requires an owner and classification before access is granted; access to the highest-classification repositories routes through the access-request workflow rather than ad-hoc sharing.
outcome_lens: Least privilege extended from applications to the unstructured-data estate; ownerless and open repositories eliminated

story: As an identity-governance owner I want every autonomous AI agent operating against enterprise systems to be a registered, governed object — with a named human owner, a declared purpose and a scoped, least-privilege set of tool entitlements recorded before the agent is allowed to act — so that no unowned or undeclared agent holds standing access.
acceptance_criteria: An inventory of autonomous agents exists with a named human owner, declared purpose and recorded tool-scope per agent, and inventory coverage is measured and trending up; an agent cannot obtain or retain access without a registered owner and purpose; agent tool-scopes are least-privilege by default and over-broad scopes are flagged; registration is required before first action, not retrofitted.
outcome_lens: Every autonomous agent is owned, declared and least-privilege before it acts

story: As a risk owner I want an agent's tool-scopes and downstream permissions to be recertified on a risk cadence and — because an agent's effective permissions change dynamically as it is re-prompted and re-tooled — for point-in-time recertification to be augmented by continuous attestation, so that an agent's live authority never silently exceeds what was certified.
acceptance_criteria: Agent entitlements are recertified by the owner on a risk-tiered cadence and revocations are actioned within SLA; effective agent authority (granted tool-scopes plus inherited service-account / OAuth scopes) is resolvable; drift between certified and live agent authority is detected continuously and alerted, with continuous attestation modelled as the good end-state rather than periodic-only recert; excessive-agency conditions (autonomy or permissions beyond purpose) are surfaced.
outcome_lens: Agent authority is recertified and continuously attested against its declared purpose

story: As a governance owner I want decommissioned or owner-less autonomous agents — and the standing consent grants and credentials they leave behind — to be detected and revoked, so that orphaned agents do not persist as durable account-independent access (the agentic analogue of the dormant/orphan finding).
acceptance_criteria: Agents whose owner has left or whose purpose has ended are detected within a defined window and deprovisioned, including revocation of their OAuth consent grants, tool-scopes and issued credentials; orphan-agent population is a tracked KPI and trends down; a decommissioned agent leaves no residual standing access surviving its removal.
outcome_lens: No decommissioned or owner-less agent retains standing access
